catalogue_claim.text: Critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres for \(0\lt q\le4\) and to the Brownian continuum random tree for q > 4, establishing the surface-to-tree geometric transition. For FK–Ising and spanning-tree-weighted maps, stationary random walks converge to Liouville Brownian motion on the limiting sphere. The FK–Ising spectral result also gives convergence of eigenvalues and heat traces, using the stated Brownian/LQG inputs. ([Lean](lean/docs/211.md))

value.quote: For every fixed $q>4$, the formalization proves the Brownian continuum-random-tree limit for critical finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps. After rescaling graph distances in an $n$-edge map by a constant depending on $q$ times $n^{-1/2}$ and using normalized degree measure, the metric-measure space converges in distribution to the Brownian continuum random tree in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology. The convergence holds through all positive integer sizes.

statements.name: thm:main
statements.section_title: Introduction
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
For every fixed real $q>4$, there is a deterministic constant
$c(q)\in(0,\infty)$ such that, as $n\to\infty$ through all positive
integers,
\[
 \big(V(M_n),c(q)n^{-1/2}d_n,\mu_n\big)
 \ \Longrightarrow\ (\mathcal T_e,d_e,\mu_e)
\]
in the Gromov--Hausdorff--Prokhorov topology on compact metric probability
spaces modulo measure-preserving isometry.
